title: Text 3
subtitle: NHS 与 DeepMind 的数据隐私之争

sentences.en: Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain's National Health Service (NHS) and DeepMind must start by acknowledging that both sides mean well.
sentences.zh: 任何对英国国家医疗服务体系（NHS）与DeepMind之间交易风险所作的公正评估，都必须首先承认双方都是出于好意。

sentences.en: DeepMind is one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) companies in the world.
sentences.zh: DeepMind是全球领先的人工智能公司之一。

sentences.en: The potential of this work applied to healthcare is very great, but it could also lead to further concentration of power in the tech giants.
sentences.zh: 将这项工作应用于医疗保健的潜力非常巨大，但这也可能导致权力进一步集中于科技巨头手中。

sentences.en: It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1.6 million patients in 2015 on the basis of a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients' rights and their expectations of privacy.
sentences.zh: 正是在这一背景下，信息专员伊丽莎白·德纳姆对NHS下属的皇家自由医院信托基金作出了措辞严厉的裁决：该医院信托基金2015年依据一项含糊的协议，将160万患者的病历交给了DeepMind，而该协议对患者的权利及其隐私期望考虑得太少。

sentences.en: DeepMind has almost apologized.
sentences.zh: DeepMind已近乎道歉。

sentences.en: The NHS trust has mended its ways.
sentences.zh: NHS信托基金已改过自新。

sentences.en: Further arrangements — and there may be many — between the NHS and DeepMind will be carefully scrutinised to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned.
sentences.zh: NHS与DeepMind之间进一步（而且可能还会有很多）的合作安排将受到仔细审查，以确保已征得患者所有必要的许可，并清除所有不必要的数据。

sentences.en: There are lessons about informed patient consent to learn.
sentences.zh: 在患者知情同意方面，有教训值得吸取。

sentences.en: But privacy is not the only angle in this case and not even the most important.
sentences.zh: 但隐私并非此案唯一的视角，甚至不是最重要的视角。

sentences.en: Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it "controlled" the data and DeepMind merely "processed" it.
sentences.zh: 德纳姆女士选择将责任集中在NHS信托基金身上，因为根据现行法律，它“控制”了这些数据，而DeepMind只是“处理”了这些数据。

sentences.en: But this distinction misses the point that it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession of bits, that gives the data value.
sentences.zh: 但这种区分忽略了这样一个要点：赋予数据价值的正是处理与整合，而非仅仅占有数据位。

sentences.en: The great question is who should benefit from the analysis of all the data that our lives now generate.
sentences.zh: 最大的问题是，谁应该从对我们生活所产生的所有数据的分析中获益。

sentences.en: Privacy law builds on the concept of damage to an individual from identifiable knowledge about them.
sentences.zh: 隐私法建立在“可识别身份的信息会对个人造成损害”这一概念之上。

sentences.en: That misses the way the surveillance economy works.
sentences.zh: 这忽略了监控经济的运作方式。

sentences.en: The data of an individual there gains its value only when it is compared with the data of countless millions more.
sentences.zh: 在监控经济中，个人的数据只有在与千百万其他人的数据进行比较时才有价值。

sentences.en: The use of privacy law to curb the tech giants in this instance feels slightly maladapted.
sentences.zh: 在此案中运用隐私法来约束科技巨头，感觉有些不太合适。

sentences.en: This practice does not address the real worry.
sentences.zh: 这种做法并没有解决真正的担忧。

sentences.en: It is not enough to say that the algorithms DeepMind develops will benefit patients and save lives.
sentences.zh: 仅仅说DeepMind开发的算法将使患者受益并拯救生命，这是不够的。

sentences.en: What matters is that they will belong to a private monopoly which developed them using public resources.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，这些算法将属于一家利用公共资源开发它们的私人垄断企业。

sentences.en: If software promises to save lives on the scale that drugs now can, big data may be expected to behave as a big pharma has done.
sentences.zh: 如果软件能像现在的药物那样有望大规模拯救生命，那么大数据的表现或许就会像大型制药公司一样。

sentences.en: We are still at the beginning of this revolution and small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later.
sentences.zh: 我们仍处于这场革命的起步阶段，现在的一些小选择，将来可能会产生巨大的后果。

sentences.en: A long struggle will be needed to avoid a future of digital feudalism.
sentences.zh: 要避免数字封建主义的未来，需要长期的努力。

sentences.en: Ms Denham's report is a welcome start.
sentences.zh: 德纳姆女士的报告是一个值得欢迎的开端。

questions.stem: What is true of the agreement between the NHS and DeepMind?

options.A: It caused conflicts among tech giants.
options.B: It failed to pay due attention to patients’ rights.
options.C: It fell short of the latter’s expectations.
options.D: It put both sides into a dangerous situation.

questions.analysis: 细节题。根据题干中的NHS， DeepMind和agreement回文定位第一段第四句“It is against that background that the information commissioner， has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS， which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1.6 million patients in 2015 on the basis of a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients’ rights and their expectations of privacy”。根据a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients’ rights and their expectations of privacy这一部分的语义信息，说明NHS与DeepMind之间的协议没有充分考虑到病人的权利与隐私。这句话的言外之意就是协议未能充分关注病人的权利。故确定答案为选项B，其中failed to是took far too little account的同义改写。

questions.stem: The NHS trust responded to Denham’s verdict with ____
questions.analysis: 细节题。根据题干中的NHS trust， 以及Denham’s verdict回文定位第二段第二句“The NHS trust has mended its ways。” 根据第二句的语义信息，NHS trust针对Denham’s verdict已经调整了其与DeepMind的协议内容，故通过同义替换，可确定正确答案为C。

questions.stem: The author argues in Paragraph 2 that ____

options.A: privacy protection must be secured at all costs.
options.B: leaking patients’ data is worse than selling it.
options.C: making profits from patients’ data is illegal.
options.D: the value of data comes from the processing of it.

questions.analysis: 推理题。根据题干，此题定位在第二段最后一句but之后的转折句。“But this distinction misses the point that it is processing and aggregation， not the mere possession of bits， that gives data value”。 这种区分忽视了一个点：是处理和收集赋予数据意义，而不是拥有数据。 选项中的 “processing”和原文中的“processing”原词复现。 选项中的“the value of data”对应原文中的“data value”。因此，D项为正确答案。

questions.stem: According to the last paragraph, the real worry arising from this deal is ____

options.A: the vicious rivalry among big pharmas.
options.B: the ineffective enforcement of privacy law.
options.C: the uncontrolled use of new software.
options.D: the monopoly of big data by tech giants.

questions.analysis: 细节题。根据题干此题定位在文中最后一段的第四句。“What matters is that they will belong to a private monopoly which developed them using public resources。”重要的是这些进步属于一个私人垄断企业，而私人垄断企来使用公共资源进行研发。而这正真正的担忧所在。因此，选项D为正确答案， the monopoly of big data by tech giants对应原文中的a private monopoly。

questions.stem: The author’s attitude toward the application of AI to healthcare is ____
questions.analysis: 态度题。本题考查作者对本文主题“将人工智能应用于医疗健康”的态度。根据顺序性原则定位在最后一段。该段倒数第三句话指出“我们目前依然处于这一改革的前期，并且任何小的选择都会对未来产生深远的影响”，其中“still”一词，以及“small”（小）和“gigantic”（巨大的）对比，都体现出了作者对待整个事件是小心谨慎的态度，因此[B] cautious为正确答案。
